title: FUT national mobilization for public social security: Quito afternoon march
location: Quito: from the IESS Caja del Seguro to the historic center and Plaza Sixto Durán Ballén
participants_original: EFE reports “cientos de trabajadores” marching through central Quito; qualitative estimate, not an exact count.
threshold_50_evidence: S009 (Agencia EFE) reports hundreds of workers in this January 19 Quito march, supporting a simultaneous gathering above 50. It gives no exact count, numeric range, or site-by-site estimate. Do not pool this march with the separately reported morning sit-in.

occurrence.summary: Both opened reports describe a FUT march in Quito on January 19; S001 places its call at 16:00 and S009 reports the march through central Quito.

start_date.summary: Both opened reports date the march to January 19, 2023.

end_date.summary: S001 says the march reached Plaza Sixto Durán Ballén after 17:00 and made a statement there, but does not say when participants dispersed.

location.summary: S001 traces the march from the IESS Caja toward the historic center and Plaza Sixto Durán Ballén; S009 reports the route from the IESS toward central Quito.

scope.summary: S001 calls the FUT mobilization national. The opened reports document the physical march and attendance in Quito only; the national label does not establish attendance in other cities.

organizer.summary: Both reports identify the Frente Unitario de Trabajadores (FUT) as the convener.

demands.summary: Reports identify opposition to proposed IESS/pension reforms and the government commission, demands concerning IESS leadership and government debt to the IESS, and defense of the public social-security model.

participants_original.summary: EFE reports “cientos de trabajadores” in the Quito march; the report supplies no exact count.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: The qualitative report of hundreds describes one march through Quito and supports more than 50 participants; it does not support a numeric interval or other-city count.

state_target.summary: Demands addressed Ecuador's government and its IESS/pension-reform process, including IESS leadership and government debt to the IESS.

protester_violence.summary: These accounts do not describe event-specific violence by protesters. Violence remains unknown; silence is not coded as absence.

state_response.summary: The reports do not establish an event-specific state response after the march. S001 reports a commission coordinator's invitation to meet on January 18, before the march; it is not coded as a response to the event. All response dimensions remain unknown.

notes: Keep the Quito morning sit-in in E002 as a separate physical action and do not pool its attendance. The “national” scope reflects S001's description of the mobilization, while the opened reports verify the Quito march only.
open_questions: What time did the march physically end or disperse?

title: FUT leaders' morning sit-in at the IESS Directing Council
location: Outside Edificio Zarzuela, where the IESS Directing Council meets, Quito
participants_original: S001 describes the main FUT leaders holding a morning sit-in; it gives no attendee count.
threshold_50_evidence: The opened account identifies only the main FUT leaders and supplies no number of simultaneous people at the site. Do not infer 50 participants from the number of FUT organizations or from the separate afternoon march.

occurrence.summary: S001 separately describes a morning FUT sit-in outside the IESS Directing Council building.

start_date.summary: The report places the sit-in on the morning of January 19, 2023.

end_date.summary: The report does not identify when the sit-in ended or participants dispersed.

location.summary: The account places the sit-in outside Edificio Zarzuela, where the IESS Directing Council meets.

scope.summary: Only this Quito site is described for the sit-in.

organizer.summary: The report attributes the action to FUT leaders.

demands.summary: FUT leaders sought council appointments for two named representatives and a comprehensive IESS reform benefiting affiliates and retirees.

participants_original.summary: The report says the main leaders attended but gives no number of people at the site.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: No attendee estimate establishes 50 simultaneous participants; the afternoon march's reported attendance is kept separate.

state_target.summary: The sit-in took place outside the public IESS governing council and addressed appointments and IESS reform.

protester_violence.summary: The account does not describe event-specific violence by protesters. Violence remains unknown.

state_response.summary: The FUT president says an earlier dialogue proposal was ignored, while S001 also reports a commission coordinator's January 18 invitation to meet. These are temporally distinct, source-attributed statements and do not establish a state response to the January 19 sit-in; every response dimension remains unknown.

notes: This morning sit-in is a distinct physical action from E001's afternoon march. Do not pool attendance. The article does not establish whether participants overlapped or whether both actions were treated as one event.
open_questions: Were at least 50 people simultaneously present at the sit-in?
When did the sit-in physically end?

title: Cetrapep protest outside Petroecuador offices over wage equalization and working conditions
location: Outside Petroecuador's offices on Alpallana Street, north Quito
organizer: Comité de Empresa de los Trabajadores de Petroecuador (Cetrapep)
participants_original: S003 identifies protesting Petroecuador workers but gives no attendee count or estimate at the office site.
threshold_50_evidence: S003 reports workers protesting outside the offices from January 18 through January 20, but gives no number of simultaneous participants at that site. Eligibility remains pending the 50-person threshold.

occurrence.summary: S003 reports Cetrapep members protesting outside Petroecuador's Quito offices.

start_date.summary: S003 says the workers began protesting on January 18, 2023.

end_date.summary: Workers said on January 20 that they had ended protests after three days; the physical end is recorded as January 20, without an hour.

location.summary: S003 places the protest outside the state oil company's offices on Alpallana Street in north Quito.

scope.summary: The report describes one local protest site at the company's Quito offices.

organizer.summary: The report identifies the workers as members of Cetrapep.

demands.summary: The report describes demands to implement a court ruling on equalizing wages, address company administrative practices, and improve work conditions and transport.

participants_original.summary: The report identifies protesting workers but gives no number of people present.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: No event-site attendance estimate establishes at least 50 simultaneous participants.

state_target.summary: The target was Petroecuador, which the report identifies as a state oil company; the report also names EMCO, the public-enterprise coordinator, in the company's account of an agreement. This target coding is retained for coordinator review.

protester_violence.summary: S003 does not describe event-specific violence by protesters; violence remains unknown rather than coded absent.

state_response.accommodation.summary: Petroecuador said the union reached an agreement with EMCO and that the company was renewing vehicles and providing work clothes. The union did not immediately comment; accommodation is coded yes as the company's attributed account, not as a verified victory.

state_response.summary: The company reports the EMCO agreement, but S003 does not report arrests, beatings, dispersal, or killings/shootings. Those dimensions remain unknown; silence is not treated as no.

notes: The company says the protest did not affect operations and attributes the EMCO agreement and vehicle/workwear measures to its response. No union confirmation or attendee count is reported.
open_questions: How many people were simultaneously present at the protest site?
Does the public-enterprise employer target satisfy the baseline government-target rule for this labor dispute?
